questions.corrige_markdown:
The expected value (mean) of a discrete random variable is the probability-weighted sum of its values:

$$E(X) = \sum_i x_i\, f(x_i) = \sum_i x_i\, P(X = x_i)$$

where the sum runs over all possible values $x_i$ of $X$.

The variance is the expected squared deviation from the mean, $\mu = E(X)$:

$$Var(X) = E\big[(X - \mu)^2\big] = \sum_i (x_i - \mu)^2 f(x_i)$$

or, in the form used for calculation,

$$Var(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = \sum_i x_i^2\, f(x_i) - \left[\sum_i x_i\, f(x_i)\right]^2$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(ii)** A function $f$ defined on the set $\{1, m, 6, 8, 12\}$ is given by the table below.

| $x$ | 1 | $m$ | 6 | 8 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | 0.1 | 0.3 | 0.2 | $n$ | 0.15 |

If $f$ is the probability mass function of the random variable $X$ and $E(X) = 6.0$, calculate,

(a) the values of the constants $m$ and $n$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Finding $n$.** The probabilities of a probability mass function sum to 1:

$$0.1 + 0.3 + 0.2 + n + 0.15 = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; 0.75 + n = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; n = 0.25$$

**Finding $m$.** Use $E(X) = \sum x\, f(x) = 6$:

$$1(0.1) + m(0.3) + 6(0.2) + 8(0.25) + 12(0.15) = 6$$

$$0.1 + 0.3m + 1.2 + 2 + 1.8 = 6 \;\Rightarrow\; 5.1 + 0.3m = 6 \;\Rightarrow\; 0.3m = 0.9 \;\Rightarrow\; m = 3$$

**$m = 3$ and $n = 0.25$.**
